ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a voltage-commutated chopper circuit, the left DC power supply is labeled V = 250 V; the commutating capacitor is labeled 1 µF; the commutating inductor is labeled 2 mH; in the figure the main switch M, auxiliary switch A, diode branches, and the DC load with an inductor on the right side can also be seen, and the load current direction is labeled i_L. Reasoning: The problem statement gives the chopper operating frequency f = 1 kHz, therefore the period T = 1/f = 1 ms. The load current is assumed constant as I_L = 10 A. According to the standard conduction pulse-width expression of the voltage-commutated chopper, t_p = π√(LC) + 2CV_s/I_L. Substituting L = 2 mH = 2×10^-3 H, C = 1 µF = 1×10^-6 F, V_s = 250 V, I_L = 10 A: π√(LC) = π√(2×10^-3 × 1×10^-6) ≈ 0.140 ms; 2CV_s/I_L = 2×1×10^-6×250/10 = 0.050 ms. So t_p ≈ 0.190 ms. The average output voltage V_avg = V_s(t_p/T) = 250×(0.190/1) ≈ 47.5 V. The final answer rounded to one decimal place is 47.5.
